name: Hani
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Li Yongsui & Wang Ersong (1986) Haniyu Jianzhi [A Sketch of the Hani Language] - print only, phonology sketch of this tonal language

sources.citation: Hansson, Inga-Lill. 1982. A phonological comparison of Akha and Hani. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 7(1): 63-115.
sources.note: Silent. Segmental and tonal comparison of Lüchun Hani (1959 Hani-Chinese wordlist + 1981 tape) with Akha; describes 3 tones (High -l, Mid -zero, Low -q) plus laryngealized Mid -v / Low -vq. No occurrence of 'stress', 'accent' or 'prominence' in the 53 scanned pages.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2002. The Central and Southern Loloish languages of Vietnam. Proceedings of BLS 28, Special Session on Tibeto-Burman and Southeast Asian Linguistics: 1-13. DOI 10.3765/bls.v28i2.1042
sources.note: Section 5 'Hani (Hahni)' (pp. 8-11) gives Vietnam Hani (Muong Te) tones 55/31/33 plus two glottally constricted syllable shapes [31ʔ] [33ʔ], initials, and comparisons with Lüchun Hani and Akha; nothing on stress. The one 'first syllable is often unstressed' remark (p. 3) concerns Cóong (Bisoid), not Hani.

sources.citation: Hansson, Inga-Lill. 1989. A comparison of Akha, Hani, Khatu and Pijo. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 12(1): 6-91.
sources.note: Silent in the introductory and phonological-overview pages (pp. 1-20 scanned); comparative wordlist study of Akha (Thailand/Yunnan), Hani, Khatu, Pijo. Remaining pages (21-86, wordlist appendices) not scanned.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Hani language'; Wikipedia (zh) '哈尼语'; Wikipedia (vi) 'Tiếng Hà Nhì' (phonology sections, citing Li & Wang 1986)
sources.note: Tones only (55, 33, 31, and 24 in recent Chinese loans; laryngealized 'buzzing' vowels); no statement on stress in any of the three language editions.

sources.citation: Wheatley, Julian K. 1982. Comments on the 'Hani' dialects of Loloish. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 7(1): 1-37.
sources.note: Silent. Historical-phonological subgrouping of Hani dialects (initials, glottal stricture, tones); no mention of stress or accent in 38 scanned pages.

sources.citation: Tạ Văn Thông & Lê Đông. 2001. Tiếng Hà Nhì. Hà Nội: Nhà xuất bản Văn hóa dân tộc.

sources.note: Vietnamese description of Hà Nhì (Vietnam Hani, Muong Te/Bat Xat); Vietnamese-language sketches conventionally have a 'trọng âm' remark in the ngữ âm chapter.

sources.note: Standard reference sketch of Lüchun Hani; its 语音 chapter (声母/韵母/声调/音节/语音变化) is the most likely place for a statement on 轻重音 or an explicit remark that Hani has no lexical stress. Named by the earlier world scan; Wikipedia phonology sections derive from it.
